requirements.title: LLE argument restrictions
requirements.definition: STRING_A shall be default character or ASCII character, and STRING_B shall be character with the same kind type parameter as STRING_A.

pending.LLE-STRING_A-default-or-ASCII-character: Positive source controls call LLE with default CHARACTER STRING_A and same-kind character STRING_B; source-control mutations use a noncharacter actual and claim no diagnostic facet.
pending.LLE-STRING_B-same-character-kind: Positive source controls call LLE with same-kind default CHARACTER arguments; a source-control mutation uses different character kinds and claims no diagnostic facet.

requirements.title: LLE uses blank padding and ASCII less-than-or-equal result semantics
requirements.definition: For ASCII strings, unequal lengths are compared after right blank padding of the shorter string; LLE is true for equal strings or for STRING_A preceding STRING_B in the ASCII collating sequence, and false otherwise.

pending.LLE-unequal-length-blank-padding: Initialize logical results to opposite sentinels and keep the length-discriminating cases: assert LLE("A","A ") is true because the shorter left operand is right-padded with ASCII blank 32, and assert LLE("A!","A ") is false because ASCII exclamation 33 follows blank 32. Mutate the second operand blank to "!" or swap operands so the comparison changes.
pending.LLE-equal-strings-true: Assert LLE("AZ","AZ") and LLE("","") are true with .false. sentinels; mutate LLE to LLT so the equality cases fail.
pending.LLE-ascii-precedes-true: Assert ASCII-table discriminators with .false. sentinels: LLE("9","A") is true because ASCII 57 precedes 65, LLE("A","a") is true because ASCII 65 precedes 97, LLE("Z","a") is true because ASCII 90 precedes 97, and LLE("Z","_") is true because ASCII 90 precedes 95. Also retain LLE("ONE","TWO") as the example-derived same-case control. Reverse each discriminator in companion false checks so ASCII collating sequence, not native character order, is load-bearing.
pending.LLE-ascii-follows-false: Assert reversed ASCII-table discriminators with .true. sentinels: LLE("A","9") is false because ASCII 65 follows 57, LLE("a","A") is false because ASCII 97 follows 65, LLE("a","Z") is false because ASCII 97 follows 90, and LLE("_","Z") is false because ASCII 95 follows 90. Also assert LLE("B","A") is false as a same-case control; swap operands so each false case becomes true.

requirements.title: LLE non-ASCII comparison result is processor dependent
requirements.definition: A LLE comparison result is processor dependent once either string contains a character outside the ASCII character set.

pending.LLE-non-ASCII-result-processor-dependent: No portable oracle for a fixed truth value: p5 makes any result processor dependent once either string contains a non-ASCII character; future exact LLE fixtures restrict operands to ASCII characters.
